abandon.meaning: To leave someone or something behind.
abandon.clue: The sailors had to abandon the damaged ship.

abundance.meaning: A very large amount of something; more than enough.
abundance.clue: There was an abundance of cake at the birthday party.

affable.meaning: Friendly, pleasant, and easy to get along with.
affable.clue: Henry, an affable child, always included anyone who was being left out of the conversation.

antiquity.meaning: Ancient times; or an object that has survived from ancient times.
antiquity.clue: The ancient Greek vase was the museum's most precious antiquity.

arduous.meaning: Difficult, tiring, and requiring a lot of effort.
arduous.clue: Building a brick wall is an arduous task.

assiduous.meaning: Working hard and carefully, and not giving up.
assiduous.clue: Jenny was an assiduous candidate during her election campaign for school captain.

avowed.clue: The boy's avowed ambition was to become an excellent mathematician.

barren.meaning: Unable to grow plants; empty and bare.
barren.clue: Very little could grow on the barren land.

belligerent.clue: The belligerent man began shouting at everyone in the room.

besieged.meaning: Surrounded by attackers; also faced with too many demands or problems.
besieged.clue: The besieged city waited anxiously for help while enemy troops blocked every road.

bewildered.meaning: Very confused and unable to understand what is happening.
bewildered.clue: Mia looked bewildered when she saw the complicated instructions.

choreographer.meaning: Someone who plans the steps of a dance.

composition.meaning: Something made by putting parts together, such as music or a piece of writing.

comrade.meaning: A friend who shares your work or experiences.
comrade.clue: The soldier refused to leave his injured comrade behind.

conscience.meaning: Your inner sense of right and wrong.
conscience.clue: His conscience told him that he should admit that he had broken the window.

contemporary.meaning: From the present time; also living at the same time as someone else.
contemporary.clue: The gallery displays contemporary British art.

conventional.meaning: Following the usual way of doing things.
conventional.clue: They chose a conventional design for their new house.

covet.meaning: To want something that belongs to someone else very much.

coy.meaning: Shy, or not wanting to give much away.

deceive.meaning: To make someone believe something that is not true.
deceive.clue: The dishonest salesman tried to deceive his customers.

demolished.clue: The old factory was demolished to make room for new houses.

destitute.meaning: So poor that you lack basics such as food and a home.
destitute.clue: The charity provides food and shelter for destitute families.

dilapidated.meaning: Old and falling apart because it has not been looked after.
dilapidated.clue: They discovered a dilapidated cottage at the edge of the woods.

diluted.meaning: Made weaker by adding water or another substance.

disarray.clue: After the children had finished playing, the room was in disarray.

disastrous.clue: The expedition had a disastrous ending when a storm destroyed their supplies.

dishevelled.meaning: Looking untidy, especially your hair or clothes.
dishevelled.clue: He looked dishevelled after spending the night sleeping on the train.

dismal.clue: The team gave a dismal performance and lost badly.

disperse.meaning: To scatter or spread in different directions.
disperse.clue: The crowd began to disperse after the concert ended.

drought.meaning: A long time with hardly any rain.

embarrass.meaning: To make someone feel awkward or ashamed.

endeavour.meaning: A determined attempt to do something.
endeavour.clue: Climbing the mountain was a difficult endeavour.

enterprise.meaning: A business, or a project you work hard on.
enterprise.clue: Setting up her own bakery was an ambitious enterprise.

errand.meaning: A short journey made to deliver, collect, or do something.
errand.clue: Mum sent me on an errand to buy some milk.

evident.clue: It was evident from his smile that he was delighted.

explanation.meaning: Something that helps you understand how or why.
explanation.clue: The teacher gave a simple explanation of how the machine worked.

famine.meaning: An extreme shortage of food affecting many people.
famine.clue: The failed harvest led to a severe famine.

fatigue.meaning: Feeling very tired after hard work.
fatigue.clue: After hours of walking, she was overcome with fatigue.

feign.meaning: To pretend you have a feeling or problem.
feign.clue: He tried to feign illness so that he could avoid school.

flamboyant.meaning: Bright, bold or showy in a way that gets noticed.
flamboyant.clue: The actor arrived wearing a flamboyant purple suit.

fleet.meaning: A group of ships or vehicles working together.
fleet.clue: A fleet of fishing boats sailed out of the harbour.

frivolous.meaning: Silly or not very serious or important.

gratitude.clue: He expressed his gratitude to the stranger who had helped him.

gregarious.clue: Mia is gregarious and enjoys meeting new people.

grotesque.meaning: Very strange or ugly, sometimes in a frightening way.
grotesque.clue: A grotesque stone creature was carved above the doorway.

helix.meaning: A spiral shape, like a coil or corkscrew.

hygienic.meaning: Clean and unlikely to cause illness or spread germs.
hygienic.clue: Washing your hands before preparing food is hygienic.

idiosyncrasy.meaning: An unusual habit or feature that makes someone different.

immerse.meaning: To put completely under liquid; also to give something all your attention.
immerse.clue: She liked to immerse herself in a good book.

impudent.meaning: Rude and showing a lack of respect.

inaugural.meaning: The first event or the start of something.

inconspicuous.clue: The spy wore plain clothes to remain inconspicuous.

innocuous.clue: The spider looked frightening but was completely innocuous.

insolent.meaning: Rude and showing a lack of respect.

lament.clue: The villagers lamented the loss of the ancient woodland.

lavish.clue: They prepared a lavish feast for the celebration.

malady.clue: The doctor searched for a cure for the mysterious malady.

matte.clue: She chose matte paint because she did not want the wall to shine.

meagre.meaning: A very small amount, often not enough.

melancholy.clue: A feeling of melancholy came over him as he remembered his old home.

merchant.meaning: Someone who buys and sells things.

meticulous.meaning: Very careful about every small detail.

nauseous.meaning: Feeling as if you might be sick.

nimble.meaning: Able to move quickly, lightly, and easily.

nuisance.meaning: Someone or something that causes trouble or annoyance.

obstinate.meaning: Refusing to change your mind or behaviour.

omen.meaning: A sign people believe tells them what will happen.

oppress.meaning: To use power to treat people cruelly or unfairly.

ordeal.meaning: A very difficult or unpleasant experience.

ostentatious.meaning: Showing off money or importance to get noticed.
ostentatious.clue: He arrived in an ostentatious limousine covered in gold decorations.

palaeontologist.meaning: A scientist who studies fossils and ancient forms of life.
palaeontologist.clue: The palaeontologist carefully examined the dinosaur fossil.

peril.clue: The climbers were in great peril when the storm struck.

perish.meaning: To die or be completely destroyed.

pioneer.meaning: Someone who is one of the first to try or discover something new.

placid.meaning: Calm, peaceful, and not easily disturbed.

polarity.meaning: Having two opposite sides or qualities.

pompous.meaning: Behaving as though you are more important than you really are.

precarious.meaning: Not safe or steady, and likely to go wrong.

prohibit.meaning: To say officially that something is not allowed.

provoke.meaning: To cause a reaction, often by annoying someone.

quaint.clue: We stayed in a quaint cottage in a small village.

quench.meaning: To satisfy thirst or put out a fire.

raiment.meaning: Clothes, especially smart or special ones.

reprimand.meaning: To tell someone off seriously for doing something wrong.

restrain.meaning: To hold someone or something back or keep it under control.

rigid.meaning: Stiff and hard to bend; also unwilling to change.

scanty.meaning: Not much; less than is needed.

scripture.meaning: Writings that a religion considers holy.

seize.meaning: To grab something firmly or take it by force.

sermon.meaning: A talk about religion or how people should behave.

stern.clue: The teacher gave the class a stern warning about their behaviour.

submissive.meaning: Ready to obey without arguing or resisting.

succumb.meaning: To give in; also to die from an illness or injury.

tempestuous.meaning: Full of strong feelings, arguments or violent storms.

tranquil.clue: The garden was tranquil in the early morning.

turbulent.meaning: Full of disorder, conflict or rough movement.

vicarious.meaning: Felt through someone else's experience rather than your own.

virtuous.meaning: Behaving in a good and honest way.

wither.meaning: To dry up or become weak.

wretched.meaning: Very unhappy or in a very poor state.

abode.meaning: A place where someone lives; a home.

absurd.meaning: So silly or unreasonable that it makes no sense.

adhere.meaning: To stick to something; also to follow a rule or belief.
adhere.clue: Everyone must adhere to the safety rules.

advice.meaning: Suggestions about what you could do.

ancient.meaning: From a very long time ago.

apparent.meaning: Easy to see; sometimes, seeming to be true.

banish.meaning: To send someone away from a place as a punishment; to get rid of something.

beck.meaning: A movement that calls someone over. At someone’s beck and call means always ready to do what they want.

brusque.meaning: Speaking or acting in a quick, rather rude way.

calamity.meaning: A serious event that causes great damage or suffering.

caulk.meaning: To fill a gap so water or air cannot get through.

clemency.meaning: Choosing to be less harsh when you have the power to punish.

coax.meaning: To gently persuade someone to do something.

commence.clue: The ceremony will commence at ten o'clock.

complement.meaning: Something that completes or improves something else.

compliment.meaning: A polite expression of praise or admiration.
compliment.clue: He paid her a compliment on her excellent performance.

conceal.meaning: To hide something or prevent it from being seen or known.
conceal.clue: He tried to conceal the present behind his back.

conceit.clue: His conceit made him believe he was better than everyone else.

condemn.meaning: To say strongly that something is wrong; also to find someone guilty.

controversy.meaning: A subject that people publicly disagree about.

deceit.meaning: Tricking someone into believing something untrue.
deceit.clue: His deceit was discovered when the truth came out.

deliberate.meaning: Done on purpose and with thought.
deliberate.clue: Breaking the window was a deliberate act.

derelict.meaning: Abandoned and in very poor condition.
derelict.clue: The children were warned not to enter the derelict building.

despise.meaning: To strongly dislike and have no respect for someone or something.
despise.clue: She despised people who were deliberately cruel to animals.

device.meaning: Something made to do a particular job.
device.clue: The small electronic device measures temperature.

din.meaning: A loud, unpleasant noise that goes on and on.
din.clue: The din from the construction site made it difficult to concentrate.

disclose.meaning: To reveal information that was previously secret or unknown.
disclose.clue: The company refused to disclose the confidential information.

dispute.clue: The neighbours had a dispute over the boundary fence.

distress.clue: The injured animal was clearly in distress.

dwelling.meaning: A house or other place where someone lives.
dwelling.clue: The small dwelling stood beside the river.

economical.meaning: Using money, time or supplies without wasting them.
economical.clue: The small car is economical to run.

elude.meaning: To escape from or avoid someone or something, especially cleverly.
elude.clue: The thief managed to elude the police for several hours.

emerge.clue: A butterfly began to emerge from its chrysalis.

endure.meaning: To put up with something difficult; also to last a long time.
endure.clue: The explorers had to endure freezing temperatures.

evaluation.meaning: A careful judgement of how good or useful something is.
evaluation.clue: The teacher completed an evaluation of the student's work.

exaggerate.meaning: To describe something as bigger, better or worse than it really is.
exaggerate.clue: Do not exaggerate the size of the fish you caught.

extinction.meaning: The state of a species no longer existing.
extinction.clue: Habitat loss can push rare animals towards extinction.

factual.meaning: Based on facts rather than opinions or imagination.
factual.clue: The report was factual and supported by evidence.

fatal.meaning: Causing death, or causing something to fail completely.
fatal.clue: The poisonous bite can be fatal without treatment.

feeble.meaning: Weak and lacking physical strength or effectiveness.
feeble.clue: The elderly man spoke in a feeble voice.

fertile.meaning: Able to grow lots of plants or produce young.
fertile.clue: The fertile soil produced an excellent crop.

flourish.meaning: To grow or do very well.
flourish.clue: The plants began to flourish in the warm sunshine.

grave.meaning: Very serious; also a place where a dead person is buried.
grave.clue: The doctor warned that the patient was in grave danger.

grieve.meaning: To feel or express deep sadness, especially after a loss.
grieve.clue: The family needed time to grieve after their loss.

harbour.meaning: A safe, sheltered place for boats; also to keep a feeling inside.
harbour.clue: The fishing boats returned safely to the harbour.

hasty.meaning: Done too quickly and without enough thought.
hasty.clue: He made a hasty decision that he later regretted.

hindrance.meaning: Something that makes progress difficult or slows it down.
hindrance.clue: The heavy snow was a hindrance to the rescue team.

hoax.meaning: A trick that makes people believe something untrue.
hoax.clue: The supposed sighting of a monster turned out to be a hoax.

ignorant.clue: He was ignorant of the rules and accidentally broke one.

imitate.meaning: To copy someone's actions, behaviour, or appearance.
imitate.clue: The child tried to imitate the singer's voice.

inaugurate.meaning: To start something officially, often with a ceremony.
inaugurate.clue: The mayor will inaugurate the new community centre.

incision.meaning: A cut, especially one made during an operation.
incision.clue: The surgeon made a small incision in the patient's skin.

inferior.meaning: Not as good, or lower in rank.
inferior.clue: The cheaper material proved to be inferior in quality.

inhabitants.meaning: People or animals that live in a particular place.
inhabitants.clue: The island's inhabitants depend largely on fishing.

interfere.meaning: To get involved when your help is not wanted or needed.
interfere.clue: She told her brother not to interfere in her argument.

interrogate.meaning: To ask someone lots of detailed, formal questions.
interrogate.clue: The detectives began to interrogate the suspect.

isolation.meaning: Being apart from other people or things.
isolation.clue: The remote village lived in isolation for many years.

lenient.meaning: Not as strict or harsh as you might expect.
lenient.clue: The teacher was lenient and gave him another chance.

liable.meaning: Likely to do or suffer something; also responsible for it by law.
liable.clue: Drivers are liable for damage caused by their negligence.

linger.meaning: To remain somewhere longer than necessary or expected.
linger.clue: The smell of smoke continued to linger in the room.

lofty.meaning: Very high; also grand or noble.
lofty.clue: The eagle built its nest on a lofty cliff.

majestic.clue: The majestic mountains rose above the valley.

margin.meaning: An edge or border; also the amount between two scores or results.
margin.clue: She wrote a note in the margin of the page.

oblige.meaning: To make someone do something; also to help as a favour.
oblige.clue: The rules oblige everyone to wear a safety helmet.

offend.meaning: To upset or insult someone; or to break a law or rule.

opportunity.clue: She had an opportunity to perform on stage.

painstaking.meaning: Done with great care and effort.

passive.meaning: Letting things happen without trying to change them.
passive.clue: He remained passive while the others argued.

peculiar.meaning: Strange or unusual; particular to a specific person, place, or thing.
peculiar.clue: There was a peculiar smell coming from the cupboard.

perceive.clue: She perceived a slight change in his expression.

perplexed.clue: He looked perplexed by the difficult riddle.

pigment.meaning: A substance that gives colour to something.
pigment.clue: The artist mixed a blue pigment into the paint.

plunder.meaning: To steal goods by force, especially during war or disorder.
plunder.clue: The invaders began to plunder the abandoned town.

pretence.meaning: Making something seem true when it is not.
pretence.clue: He made a pretence of being asleep when his mother entered.

proclaim.meaning: To announce something publicly or officially.
proclaim.clue: The king stood before the crowd to proclaim the good news.

prophecy.meaning: A statement that predicts what will happen in the future.
prophecy.clue: According to the ancient prophecy, a great leader would arise.

relevant.meaning: Connected to what you are talking about or doing.

repent.meaning: To feel sorry for something wrong you have done and wish to change.
repent.clue: He began to repent after realising how much harm he had caused.

resort to.meaning: To try something because other ways have not worked.

retreat.meaning: To move back, often away from danger.

rowdy.clue: The rowdy crowd disturbed the neighbours.

sanguine.meaning: Hopeful and confident that things will go well.
sanguine.clue: She remained sanguine about her chances of success.

sanitary.clue: The kitchen must be kept sanitary at all times.

stationary.clue: The car remained stationary at the traffic lights.

sturdy.meaning: Strongly built and unlikely to break or be damaged.
sturdy.clue: The sturdy table easily supported the heavy boxes.

subdued.meaning: Quieter or less bright or strong than usual.
subdued.clue: The usually cheerful class was subdued after hearing the bad news.

subterfuge.meaning: A trick used to hide what you are really doing.
subterfuge.clue: He used subterfuge to conceal his true intentions.

subterranean.clue: The explorers discovered a subterranean tunnel.

summit.meaning: The top of a mountain; also a meeting of leaders.
summit.clue: The climbers finally reached the summit before noon.

superfluous.meaning: More than is needed or necessary.
superfluous.clue: Remove any superfluous details from your answer.

torment.meaning: Severe physical or mental suffering; or to cause such suffering.
torment.clue: The constant toothache was a source of torment.

trivia.meaning: Unimportant facts or details, often interesting or entertaining.
trivia.clue: The quiz included trivia about famous films.

trivial.clue: They argued over a trivial matter.

unfathomable.meaning: Very difficult or impossible to understand.

unsurpassed.meaning: As good as or better than anything else.

vanish.clue: The magician made the coin vanish.

volatile.meaning: Likely to change suddenly; also turning easily into gas.
volatile.clue: The volatile situation could become dangerous at any moment.

yacht.meaning: A boat used for fun or racing.
yacht.clue: They sailed their yacht along the coast.

yield.meaning: To produce something; also to give way or give in.

tardy.meaning: Late; not arriving or happening on time

punctual.meaning: Arriving or happening at the correct time
punctual.clue: Maya is punctual and always arrives before the bell.

deteriorate.clue: Without repairs, the old roof will continue to deteriorate.

thrive.meaning: To grow well or do very well.
thrive.clue: Tomato plants thrive in warm, sunny conditions.

imperative.clue: It is imperative that you wear a helmet while cycling.

lout.meaning: A rude, clumsy, or badly behaved person
lout.clue: The lout pushed to the front of the queue without apologising.

viscous.meaning: Thick and sticky, so it flows slowly.
viscous.clue: Honey is more viscous than water.

vicious.clue: The vicious dog snarled at anyone who approached the gate.

gravely.clue: The doctor spoke gravely about the risks of the operation.

boldness.meaning: Confidence and willingness to take risks

fortitude.clue: He showed remarkable fortitude during the difficult journey.

grit.meaning: Courage to keep trying when things are hard.

apprehension.meaning: Anxiety or fear about what may happen

rivet.clue: The storyteller managed to rivet the children's attention.

tedious.meaning: Boring because it is long or repetitive

apathy.meaning: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern

veto.meaning: To use your authority to say a plan cannot go ahead.

agitated.clue: The horse became agitated when it heard the thunder.

sanction.meaning: Official permission; also a penalty for breaking a rule.

feud.meaning: A bitter argument that lasts a long time.

savage.clue: The village was struck by a savage storm.

ferocious.clue: A ferocious wind battered the coast.

callous.meaning: Unkind and showing no concern for others

loathe.clue: He loathed getting up before sunrise.

enmity.meaning: Strong dislike between people or groups.

steadfast.clue: She remained steadfast despite pressure to change her mind.

supple.meaning: Flexible and able to bend easily

foam.clue: White foam gathered on the waves near the shore.

froth.meaning: A mass of small bubbles on a liquid

obscene.clue: The editor removed the obscene language from the article.

vulgar.clue: His vulgar joke offended several guests.

cordial.clue: The two rivals remained cordial when they met.

demolish.meaning: To completely destroy a building or structure

facile.meaning: Easy, or seeming too simple to be useful.

cinch.clue: After weeks of practice, the final routine was a cinch.

intricate.clue: The clock contained an intricate system of tiny gears.

programme.meaning: A planned set of activities or events.
programme.clue: The holiday programme included swimming, painting and a treasure hunt.

pronunciation.meaning: The way a word is spoken, including its sounds and stress.
pronunciation.clue: I listened to the recording to check the pronunciation of 'yacht'.

purpose.meaning: The reason something is done or made.
purpose.clue: The purpose of the poster was to invite people to our play.

queue.meaning: A line of people or things waiting for their turn.
queue.clue: We joined the queue for the museum's dinosaur exhibition.

recognise.meaning: To know someone or something because you have met or seen them before.
recognise.clue: I could recognise my friend's laugh even behind the curtain.

recommend.meaning: To suggest that something is a good choice.
recommend.clue: Which funny book would you recommend for our reading club?

restaurant.meaning: A place where people pay to sit and eat meals cooked for them.
restaurant.clue: We ate lunch at a restaurant beside the river.

rhyme.meaning: A match between the end sounds of words, such as 'cat' and 'hat'.
rhyme.clue: I needed a rhyme for 'moon', so I chose 'spoon'.

rhythm.meaning: A pattern of beats or sounds.
rhythm.clue: We clapped the rhythm while our friend played the drum.

sacrifice.meaning: To give up something valued for a more important reason.
sacrifice.clue: I would sacrifice some playtime to help my friend finish the model.

secretary.meaning: Someone whose work includes organising records, messages and meetings.
secretary.clue: The club secretary sent everyone the date of the next meeting.

shoulder.meaning: The part of the body where an arm joins the torso.
shoulder.clue: The parrot perched on the pirate's shoulder.

signature.meaning: Someone's name written in their own particular way.
signature.clue: The author added her signature inside my book.

simile.meaning: A comparison using 'like' or 'as' to show a shared quality.
simile.clue: We wrote the simile 'as quiet as a sleeping mouse'.

sincere.meaning: Meaning what you say or feel; not pretending.
sincere.clue: His sincere apology showed that he truly regretted breaking the toy.

sincerely.meaning: In a way that shows you really mean what you say or feel.
sincerely.clue: I sincerely hope you feel better soon.

soldier.meaning: A person who serves in an army.
soldier.clue: The soldier helped deliver supplies after the flood.

stanza.meaning: A group of lines forming a section of a poem.
stanza.clue: The poem had three stanzas; each stanza contained four lines.

stomach.meaning: The organ that receives food after it is swallowed and helps digest it.
stomach.clue: Food travels from your mouth down a tube to your stomach.

structure.meaning: The way the parts of something are arranged.
structure.clue: We planned the structure of our story before writing its opening.

sufficient.clue: We have sufficient paper for everyone to make a kite.

suggest.meaning: To put forward an idea for someone to consider.
suggest.clue: I suggest we name our cardboard robot Sir Rusty.

summarise.meaning: To give the main points in a shorter form.
summarise.clue: Please summarise the chapter in three sentences.

symbol.meaning: A mark, object or sign that represents something else.
symbol.clue: The dove is often used as a symbol of peace.

system.meaning: A set of connected parts that work together.
system.clue: The school's heating system keeps the classrooms warm.

temperature.meaning: A measure of how hot or cold something is.
temperature.clue: We used a thermometer to check the temperature of the water.

theme.meaning: A central idea explored in a piece of writing or art.
theme.clue: Friendship is a theme in the story about two lost penguins.

tone.meaning: The attitude or feeling shown by someone's voice or writing.
tone.clue: Her cheerful tone made the invitation sound welcoming.

twelfth.clue: I was twelfth in the line, with eleven people ahead of me.

variety.meaning: A range of different things or types.
variety.clue: The picnic included a variety of fruit, from apples to mangoes.

vegetable.meaning: A plant or part of a plant used as food, especially in savoury meals.
vegetable.clue: We each chose a vegetable to add to the soup.

vehicle.meaning: Something used to transport people or goods, such as a car or bus.
vehicle.clue: The delivery vehicle stopped outside the bakery.
